title: Debiased Recommendation with Noisy Feedback

problem.claim: Recommendation data are affected by missing-not-at-random ratings and inconsistency between observed ratings and users' true preferences.

gap.claim: Existing EIB, IPS, and DR methods address MNAR data but ignore noisy feedback or outcome measurement errors.

contributions.claim: Designs OME-EIB, OME-IPS, and OME-DR estimators to address outcome measurement errors in recommendation scenarios.
Provides theoretical results on the unbiasedness and generalization bound of the proposed estimators.
Proposes an alternate denoising training approach for unbiased learning under MNAR data with outcome measurement errors.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report extensive experiments on three real-world datasets and one semi-synthetic dataset showing the effectiveness of the proposed approaches.

narrative_sequence.summary: Ratings are typically missing not at random because users choose which items to rate.
Existing debiasing methods address MNAR data but overlook noisy feedback and outcome measurement errors.
The work studies unbiased learning under the intersection of MNAR data and outcome measurement errors.
It introduces OME-aware estimators, proves theoretical properties, and proposes a denoising training approach.
The authors report experiments across real-world and semi-synthetic datasets.

source_observation.claim: Observed recommendation ratings may be both selectively missing and noisy measurements of user preferences.

interpretation.claim: Debiasing methods may need to model selection bias and outcome measurement error jointly.

application.claim: When feedback is user-selected and potentially unreliable, evaluate methods that explicitly address both mechanisms.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether the proposed approaches apply beyond the reported recommendation settings.

unknowns: Details of the estimator formulations and denoising procedure are not provided.
The assumptions and exact forms of the unbiasedness and generalization results are not provided.
Dataset identities, evaluation metrics, baselines, and quantitative results are not provided.
The outcome measurement error model is not specified.
